entities.name: Abu Amra Kaysan
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abū ʿAmra Kaysān was a prominent Persian mawlā during the Second Muslim Civil War (656–661 CE), whose actions significantly impacted the regional dynamics of Islam. As a key figure in the conflict, he played a crucial role in shaping the future of the Islamic Caliphate. His leadership during this pivotal period had far-reaching consequences for the Sunni-Shia divide and the subsequent fragmentation of the Muslim world.

Kaysān's involvement in the war was marked by his loyalty to the Umayyad dynasty and his efforts to maintain order in the aftermath of the civil conflict. The outcome of his actions, however, contributed to the eventual rise of Shia Islam as a major force in the region. This legacy can still be seen in the modern-day sectarian tensions between Sunni and Shia Muslims.

The significance of Abū ʿAmra Kaysān's role in the Second Muslim Civil War is evident in the enduring impact it had on the Islamic world. His actions, though often overlooked in historical accounts, are a testament to the complexities and nuances of this period in history.
